how.title: How this score works
how.intro: The score is a transparent checklist, not an AI black box. For each technician we look at the last 8 weeks of data already in Vireek and score seven operational factors. Every point of the score is traceable to one of them.

signal.same_day_changes: Jobs moved within 24 hours of their start time.
signal.earnings_trend: Commission, tips and hourly pay in the last 4 weeks versus the 4 before.
signal.on_call_load: Days on call compared with the team average.
signal.unanswered_requests: Requests in job threads the office did not answer within 4 hours.
signal.unpaid_time: Worked hours on timesheets that were rejected.
signal.callback_rate: Return visits on this technician's completed jobs.

how.bands: 0–24 low, 25–49 elevated, 50–100 high. A factor with no data is skipped, and scores are scaled down when there is little data or the technician is new — so a new hire is never flagged on thin evidence.
how.cost: Cost if they leave is a planning estimate: $15,000 for under a year on the team, $20,000 for 1–3 years and $25,000 beyond that. Expected yearly cost multiplies it by a likelihood of leaving that rises from about 8% to 60% as the score rises. It is an estimate for planning, not a prediction about any person.
how.fairness: Age, gender, ethnicity, religion, health, disability, family status or any other protected attribute is never read or scored. Only work data is used, and only owners and managers can see scores. Use the results to fix workplace causes — not to make decisions about an individual's employment.
how.limits: Rescheduled jobs are counted for the technician currently assigned to the job. Tenure is measured from when the technician was added to Vireek.
